about: Everyday check set: 120 Sanskrit sentences and verse lines a learner or reader meets, in three groups: (a) plain prose of rising difficulty, (b) well-known verse lines and sayings with full sandhi as printed, (c) sandhi-heavy lines (long compounds, sandhi between words, avagraha present and absent, the same text with and without spaces). For each item: the pada split (pausa form; compound members joined by '-', non-final members in stem form), lemma and grammar per pada, roles and heads of the main words, and a plain English rendering. Written by Claude (an LLM), not human-verified; CC BY-SA 4.0. None of the lines is in simple_sentences.json or wellknown.json, and none is from Rāmāyaṇa Bālakāṇḍa sarga 1.

conventions.lemma: prātipadika for nominals (pronouns: तद्, यद्, किम्, इदम्, एतद्, अदस्, अस्मद्, युष्मद्); for finite verbs the dhātu with its upasargas (आगम्, उत्था); a causative is its णिजन्त stem (पायि); a participle or gerundive its kṛdanta stem (गत, आचरणीय); an absolutive or infinitive its dhātu; an avyaya itself; a compound its members' lemmas joined by '-'. Alternatives that are equally right are separated by ' | '.
conventions.grammar: terms as in the pipeline's JSON: gender case number for a nominal (no gender for अस्मद्, युष्मद् and the numerals from पञ्चन् on, which have none); lakāra person number for a finite verb, with कर्मणि for a passive (active is not written); क्त्वा / ल्यप् / तुमुन् for an absolutive or infinitive; अव्यय for an indeclinable. Alternatives separated by ' | '.
conventions.roles: role names of mayur.terms.ROLES; 'at' / 'head_at' are pada indices (null head: the sentence root).

items.english: The gods live in heaven.
When the sun has risen, the birds sing.
items.note: उदित here is उद् + इ 'risen' (the same stem is also the क्त of वद् 'spoken', which does not fit).

items.english: The student writes a letter with a pen.
The king gives clothes to the poor.
items.note: दरिद्रेभ्यः is also ablative plural; the dative is meant. यच्छति is दाण् 'give' (7.3.78); the same form from यम् 'restrain' (7.3.77) does not fit.

items.english: A river flows down from the mountain.
The pupils listen to the teacher's words.
My mother cooks food at home.
Boy, come here.
Where are you all going?
I get up early every day.
items.note: प्रतिदिनम् is an avyayībhāva (2.1.6), an indeclinable by 1.1.41, whose final member takes अम् by 2.4.83; either description is accepted.

items.english: The moon is seen by the boy.
Dharma should be practised by everyone.
The mother makes the child drink milk.
The teacher teaches the pupils the Vedas.
After bathing he has his meal.
The girl fetches the book and reads it.
items.note: पुस्तकम् is the object of both verbs; it is attached to the nearer one, आनीय.

items.english: They go to the river to drink water.

items.text: यः परिश्रमं करोति स सफलो भवति
items.english: Whoever works hard becomes successful.

items.text: यं ग्रामं त्वं गच्छसि तं ग्रामम् अहम् अपि गच्छामि
items.english: I too am going to the village you are going to.

items.text: यदि त्वं परिश्रमं करिष्यसि तर्हि सफलो भविष्यसि
items.english: If you work hard, you will succeed.

items.text: वृष्टिर्न भवति चेत् कृषका दुःखिता भवन्ति
items.english: If there is no rain, the farmers are miserable.
Which village have you come from, sir?
Don't go; stay right here.
He neither eats nor drinks.

items.text: मम द्वौ भ्रातरौ एका भगिनी च सन्ति
items.english: I have two brothers and one sister.
Five boys are playing in the playground.
Twenty students sit in the classroom.
The king's officer seizes the thief and takes him to the city.
Kṛṣṇa, dressed in yellow, plays the flute.
items.note: पीताम्बर is a bahuvrīhi 'whose garment is yellow'. वादयति is the causative of वद्; the चुरादि वद् gives the same form, so either lemma is accepted.

items.english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went to the forest.
The great king is seated on the throne.
items.note: महत् becomes महा before a member in the same case (6.3.46); राजन् takes the samāsānta टच् (5.4.91).

items.english: A blue lotus shines in the lake.
One should give according to one's means.
Rāma lived at Pañcavaṭī.
items.note: पञ्चवटी 'the five banyans' is a dvigu (2.1.52) used as a place name.

items.english: The sage remains absorbed in meditation.

words.grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्ग षष्ठी एकवचन | पुंलिङ्ग षष्ठी एकवचन

items.english: This is my friend's son.
items.note: मित्र 'friend' is neuter in classical usage and masculine in later usage; both genders are accepted.

items.english: Are you well?

items.text: पुरा अयोध्यायां दशरथो नाम राजा बभूव
items.english: Long ago there was a king in Ayodhyā named Daśaratha.

items.text: मम गृहे त्रयः पुत्राश्चतस्रः पुत्र्यश्च सन्ति
items.english: There are three sons and four daughters in my house.
items.note: चतुर् takes the feminine stem चतसृ (7.2.99).

items.text: अयं मे पुत्रः स त्वा द्रष्टुम् इच्छति
items.english: This is my son; he wants to see you.
items.note: अयम् could also qualify पुत्रः ('this son of mine'); with स starting a new clause the nominal sentence is meant. मे and त्वा are the enclitics of 8.1.22 and 8.1.23.

items.english: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits.
Do not let the fruit of work be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
items.note: भूः is लुङ् without the augment after मा (6.4.74); अकर्मन् is a नञ्-compound (2.2.6).

items.text: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय
items.english: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhanañjaya, letting go of attachment.
items.note: धनञ्जय is an epithet of Arjuna, taken as one word (an aluk compound by 6.3.70 ff.).

items.english: Just as one casts off worn-out clothes...
...and a man puts on other, new ones.

items.text: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः
items.english: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it.
items.note: एनद् is the substitute of इदम् / एतद् in a renewed mention (2.4.32, 2.4.34).

items.text: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत
items.english: Whenever dharma declines, Bhārata...
Gathered on the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus, eager to fight...
The man of faith gains knowledge.
items.note: न् before ल् becomes nasalised ल् (8.4.60 तोर्लि with the nasal kept, 8.3.4 ff.).

items.english: All this is to be dwelt in by the Lord.
items.note: ईश् m. 'lord'; the line is also printed ईशावास्यम् as one word (the Upaniṣad's title).

items.english: You are that.
items.note: तत्त्वम् 'reality' + असि is a second split; the mahāvākya is तत् त्वम् असि.

items.english: I am Brahman.
This Self is Brahman.
Consciousness is Brahman.
Speak the truth; practise dharma.
Treat your mother as a god; treat your father as a god.
items.note: मातृदेव is a bahuvrīhi 'one for whom the mother is a god'.

items.english: May he protect the two of us together; may he nourish the two of us together.
May what we two study be full of light; may we never hate each other.
Arise, awake; go to the great teachers and learn.

items.text: यत्र नार्यस्तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः
items.english: Where women are honoured, there the gods are pleased.
Whoever has intelligence has strength.
Right conduct is the highest dharma.
The wealth of learning is the chief of all wealth.

items.text: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते
items.english: Do not give way to unmanliness, Pārtha; it does not suit you.
items.note: गमः is लुङ् without the augment after मा स्म (6.4.74).

items.text: षडेते यत्र वर्तन्ते तत्र देवः सहायकृत्
items.english: Where these six are found, there God lends his help.
Gaining friends, parting friends, war, and peace too.
Even after studying the sciences people remain fools;
but the man who puts it into practice is the learned one.
One should practise dharma as though Death already had one by the hair.
One offers a young goat as the sacrifice: even a god destroys the weak.
The wise pass their time in the pleasures of poetry and learning,

items.text: पुनरपि जननं पुनरपि मरणं पुनरपि जननीजठरे शयनम्
items.english: Birth again, death again, and again lying in a mother's womb.

items.text: अस्ति दाक्षिणात्ये जनपदे महिलारोप्यं नाम नगरम्
items.english: In the southern country there is a city called Mahilāropya.

items.text: उपदेशो हि मूर्खाणां प्रकोपाय न शान्तये
items.english: Advice only angers fools; it does not calm them.

words.grammar: अव्यय | नपुंसकलिङ्ग द्वितीया एकवचन | नपुंसकलिङ्ग प्रथमा एकवचन

items.english: Giving milk to snakes only adds to their venom.
O god of the curved trunk and mighty body, bright as ten million suns,
items.note: the feminine प्रभा is shortened as the last member of a bahuvrīhi (1.2.48).

items.text: निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा
items.english: keep all my undertakings free of obstacles, O god, always.
items.note: मे may be read as genitive (with कार्येषु) or dative; निर्विघ्नम् as an adverb or as the object complement.

items.english: Lakṣmī lives at the fingertips, Sarasvatī in the middle of the hand.
items.note: वसते is ātmanepada of a parasmaipada root (an irregular, ārṣa form); it is not to be forced to a regular derivation.

items.text: तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्

words.grammar: नपुंसकलिङ्ग तृतीया एकवचन | पुंलिङ्ग तृतीया एकवचन
नपुंसकलिङ्ग तृतीया एकवचन | पुंलिङ्ग तृतीया एकवचन

items.english: Enjoy it by letting it go; do not covet anyone's wealth.
items.note: तेन त्यक्तेन is also read 'with what he has left you'; कस्य स्वित् may also be a question ('whose is wealth?').

items.english: That is whole, this is whole; from the whole the whole is drawn out.
She who is white as jasmine, the moon, frost and a string of pearls, who is clothed in white,
whose hand is graced by the fine staff of the vīṇā, who sits on a white lotus,
items.note: both compounds are bahuvrīhis with the feminine stem in -आ (4.1.4).

items.english: (I bow to) the one of peaceful form, who rests on the serpent, with a lotus at his navel, the lord of the gods,
items.note: the accusatives depend on वन्दे two lines on; नाभि becomes नाभ at the end of a compound with the samāsānta अच् (5.4.75 ff.).

items.english: Lakṣmī's beloved, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis through meditation,
items.note: the accusatives depend on वन्दे in the next line of the verse; the line alone also reads as neuter nominatives.

items.english: I bow to Viṣṇu, who removes the fear of worldly life, the one lord of all the worlds.
The elephant-faced one, attended by the hosts of spirits and others, who relishes wood-apple and rose-apple fruit,
items.note: the accusatives depend on नमामि in the next line of the verse; the line alone also reads as neuter nominatives.

items.english: the son of Umā who ends sorrow: I bow to the lotus feet of the lord of obstacles.
For a true grasp of word and meaning, (I bow to the two) joined like word and meaning,
items.note: वाच् is वाक् in a compound by 8.2.30 and वाग् before a vowel by 8.2.39.

items.english: I bow to Pārvatī and Parameśvara, the parents of the world.
One should raise oneself by oneself and not let oneself sink.
For the self alone is the self's friend, and the self alone its enemy.
Whatever the best man does, other people do just the same.
Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
Better one's own duty done imperfectly than another's done well.
Death in one's own duty is better; another's duty is fraught with danger.

items.text: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्
items.english: If you are killed you will reach heaven; if you win you will enjoy the earth.
When a man dwells on the objects of the senses, attachment to them is born.
From attachment desire is born, and from desire anger arises.
From anger comes delusion; from delusion, a confused memory.
From a lapse of memory comes the loss of reason, and with reason lost he perishes.
On hearing that, the king was delighted.
items.note: the same text as c22, written without the spaces.

items.english: On hearing that, the king was delighted.
items.note: c21 with a space wherever the sandhi allows one (त् + श् = च्छ् by 8.4.40 and 8.4.63).

items.english: On the bank of a river a certain sage practised austerities.
On the bank of a river a certain sage practised austerities.
items.note: c23 with no spaces at all.

items.english: Four boys sat down under the tree.
items.note: the genitive with अधस्तात् is by 2.3.30.

items.english: Four boys sat down under the tree.
items.note: c25 with a space wherever the sandhi allows one.

items.english: With these words he vanished.
items.note: अन्तर्धीयते 'disappears' has the passive form with the agent as subject (कर्मकर्तरि, 3.1.87).

items.english: My nature is consciousness and bliss: I am Śiva, I am Śiva.
items.note: member चित् (चिद् before a vowel, 8.2.39).

items.english: My nature is consciousness and bliss: I am Śiva, I am Śiva.
items.note: c28 printed without the avagraha.

items.english: I am not mind, intellect, ego or thought.
Then the monkey says:
Then the monkey says:
items.note: c31 printed without the avagraha.

items.english: So rise, son of Kuntī, resolved to fight.
So rise, son of Kuntī, resolved to fight.
items.note: c33 with a space wherever the sandhi allows one.

items.english: The wise who have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
items.note: ते could be तद् nominative plural; here it is the dative enclitic of युष्मद् (8.1.22).

items.english: The wise who have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
items.note: c35 with a space wherever the sandhi allows one.

items.english: I am the Self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of every being.
I am the Self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of every being.
items.note: c37 with a space wherever the sandhi allows one.

items.english: Rāma, Daśaratha's son, went to the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.
Rāma, Daśaratha's son, went to the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.
items.note: c39 with no spaces at all.
